notes: France as one trip. The database holds 622 species for France, but eBird models only 153 of them as regular (abundant to uncommon) and files many of the commonest birds as rare (Greylag Goose, Tufted Duck, Black-winged Stilt, Eurasian Curlew, Common Sandpiper, Black Woodpecker, Little Owl), and the Mediterranean, Alpine and Pyrenean specialities as very rare. The automatic cut would miss the Camargue, the Crau and the mountains, so the list is hand-picked (manual) at 252 species: what a visitor on a normal two to three week trip meets. Camargue and the Mediterranean coast: Greater Flamingo, European Bee-eater, Little Bittern, Squacco and Black-crowned Night Heron, Glossy Ibis, Collared Pratincole, Slender-billed, Mediterranean and Audouin's Gull, Gull-billed and Whiskered Tern, Great Spotted Cuckoo, Calandra Lark, Greater Short-toed Lark. Crau steppe: Little Bustard, Pin-tailed Sandgrouse, European Roller, Lesser Kestrel, Stone-curlew, Tawny Pipit, Rock Sparrow. Garrigue and cliffs: Sardinian, Western Subalpine, Spectacled, Dartford, Western Orphean and Marmora's Warbler, Blue Rock Thrush, Common Rock Thrush, Rock Bunting, Western Black-eared Wheatear, Booted Eagle, Short-toed Eagle. Pyrenees and Alps: Bearded, Griffon, Egyptian and Black Vulture, Golden Eagle, Wallcreeper, Alpine Accentor, White-winged Snowfinch, Citril Finch, Alpine Chough, Spotted Nutcracker, Rock Ptarmigan, Black Grouse, Western Capercaillie (a guided bird, kept as the target of the high forests), Ring Ouzel. Atlantic coast, Brittany and Normandy: Northern Gannet, Atlantic Puffin (Sept-Iles), Razorbill, Common Guillemot, Fulmar, Kittiwake, European Shag, Brent Goose, the waders of the Baie de Somme, Mont-Saint-Michel and the Atlantic estuaries (Red Knot, Sanderling, Grey Plover, Kentish Plover, Pied Avocet), Rock Pipit. Forests and the Loire: Black, Middle Spotted, Grey-headed and Lesser Spotted Woodpecker, Eurasian Wryneck, Little Tern and Common Tern on the river, Common Crane at Lac du Der in winter, Red-crested Pochard. Corsica: Corsican Nuthatch (the one endemic), Corsican Finch, Marmora's Warbler, Audouin's Gull, Spotless Starling, Italian Sparrow, Hooded Crow, Osprey. The widespread garden, farmland, town, wetland and woodland birds are all in, including those that eBird models as rare. Left out: vagrants (about 150 species), pelagic birds a visitor meets only on a boat (shearwaters, storm-petrels, skuas, divers), winter sea ducks and northern geese (Common Scoter, Eider, Goldeneye, Goosander, Barnacle and Bean Geese), Eurasian Eagle-Owl, Tengmalm's and Pygmy Owl, Hazel Grouse, Rock Partridge, Eurasian Three-toed and White-backed Woodpecker, Bonelli's Eagle, Black Stork, Bluethroat, Bittern, Penduline Tit, Ortolan Bunting and the escaped parrots, ducks and waxbills. Cinereous Bunting is not on the database's France list and is left out. Egyptian Goose, Mandarin Duck and Ruddy Duck are too local. Barn Owl is left out because the database lists only the American Barn Owl (Tyto furcata) for France and not the Western Barn Owl (Tyto alba) that lives there. The Corsican Nuthatch is the only endemic, so the trip has a one-bird endemics chapter with Corsica as its place; the Corsican Finch and Marmora's Warbler, shared with Sardinia, sit in their normal units. Lookalikes from home: 12 pairs where the French bird really fools a European birder (Corsican, Western Bonelli's, Yellow-legged, Mediterranean Gull, Italian Sparrow, Hooded Crow, Iberian Chiffchaff, Short-toed Treecreeper, Cirl Bunting, Pallid Swift, Spotless Starling, Willow Tit). Species left out for lack of usable photos: Thekla's Lark (the library photos cannot be told from Crested Lark with confidence). Fourteen species had no approved photo on production and got card and quiz photos picked from unreviewed candidates (Common Pheasant, European Herring Gull, Lesser Kestrel, Iberian Grey Shrike, Red-billed Chough, Spotted Nutcracker, Spectacled Warbler, Corsican Nuthatch, Spotless Starling, Rock Sparrow, White-winged Snowfinch, Corsican Finch, Citril Finch, Rock Bunting); they still need approving in the media review page.
